'''François Roddier''' (23 September 1936 – 19 August 2023) was a French physicist and astronomer.

== Biography ==
François Roddier was born in 1936 in Paris.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=François Roddier {{!}} éditions parole |url=https://www.editionsparole.fr/categorie-produit/auteurs/roddier-francois/,%20https://www.editionsparole.fr/categorie-produit/auteurs/roddier-francois/ |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=www.editionsparole.fr |language=fr-FR}}</ref> He received his [[baccalauréat]] degree in [[Lyon]] in 1954. In 1956 he received a degree from the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)]] in Physical Sciences. In 1960, he entered [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] in the Sciences of the Universe section where he completed his doctoral thesis under the direction of [[Jacques Blamont]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AstroGen – The Astronomy Genealogy Project |url=https://astrogen.aas.org/front/searchdetails.php?agnumber=51893 |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=astrogen.aas.org}}</ref> There he developed an atomic jet [[spectrograph]] and used it to study the Sun.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Roddier |first=F. |date=1 February 1965 |title=Étude à haute résolution de quelques raies de Fraunhofer par observation de la réponse optique d'un jet atomique. I. Réalisation d'un spectrographe à jet atomique. |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1965AnAp...28..463R |journal=Annales d'Astrophysique |volume=28 |pages=463 |bibcode=1965AnAp...28..463R |issn=0365-0499}}</ref> He defended his thesis in 1964. In 1965, he was named professor at the [[Université Nice-Sophia-Antipolis|Université de Nice]] where he created a department of astrophysics. He formed a research group in [[helioseismology]]. He was interested in the optical effects of atmospheric turbulence and developed high angular resolution interferometric observation methods with his spouse Claude Roddier.

In 1984, he immigrated with his family to the United States to work for the [[National Optical Astronomy Observatory]] where he participated in the development of [[adaptive optics]]. He proposed a new type of [[wavefront sensor]] called a curvature sensor. In 1988 he moved to the Institute for Astrophysics at the [[University of Hawaii]] where he created a group for the research and development of adaptive optics. This group built the first adaptive optics system based on [[Deformable mirror|bimorph deformable mirrors]] and curvature sensors. The principle would be used in the adaptive optics systems in the [[Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope]], for that of the Japanese [[Subaru Telescope]], and for the MACAO system of the [[European Southern Observatory]].

Roddier retired in December 2000 and returned to live in France.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=System: UH Institute for Astronomy Researcher Wins Prestigious Muhlmann Award of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific {{!}} University of Hawaii News |url=https://manoa.hawaii.edu/news/article.php?aId=269 |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=manoa.hawaii.edu}}</ref> During his retirement, he became interested in [[thermodynamic aspects of evolution]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gerlache |first=Jacques de |date=2023-08-29 |title=Un hommage à François Roddier, un des esprits les plus éclairants du XXème siècle |url=https://up-magazine.info/technologies-a-la-pointe/technologies/118804-un-hommage-a-francois-roddier-un-des-esprits-les-plus-eclairants-du-xxeme-siecle/ |access-date=2023-09-12 |website=UP' Magazine |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

François Roddier died on 19 August 2023, at the age of 86.<ref>[https://www.libramemoria.com/defunts/roddier-francois/e162c81f0f2848c796b6974faa7e6769 Monsieur François Roddier] {{in lang|fr}}</ref>

== Publications ==

=== Books ===
* ''The Thermodynamics of Evolution'', trans. Stephen Ridgway, Parole éditions, 2020 
* ''De la thermodynamique à l'économie. Le tourbillon de la vie'', Parole éditions, 2018
* ''Thermodynamique de l'évolution. Un essai de thermo-bio-sociologie'', Parole éditions, 2012
* ''Le pain, le levain et les gènes. Un essai sur l'évolution'', Parole éditions, 2009
* ''''Adaptive Optics in Astronomy'''' (in collaboration with ten other authors), ''Cambridge University Press'', 1999
* ''Distributions et Transformation de Fourier'', Ediscience (1971, 1978), McGraw Hill (1984, 1988, 1993).

== Honors and awards ==
* 1965 – Houlevigue Prize from [[French Academy of Sciences]]
* 1978 – Deslandres Prize from the French Academy of Sciences
* 1991 – Fellow member, American Optical Society
* 1992 – Médaille de l'ADION, [[Nice Observatory]]
* 1993 – [[Prix Jules Janssen]] from the [[Société astronomique de France]]
* 1996 – André Lallemand prize  from the French Academy of Sciences
* 2000 – ''Board of  Regents Medal of Excellence in Research'', [[University of Hawaiʻi|University of Hawaii]]
* 2002 – Maria and Eric Muhlmann Prize from the [[Astronomical Society of the Pacific]]<ref name=":1" />
